coaching.summary: The core tension is between Nursing Staffing Adequacy through fast-acting Travel-Nurse Staffing Spend and sustainable Nurse Retention Rate through Wage and Retention Investment, both constrained by the $8M annual budget cap and the hard requirement that Patient Safety Metric Degradation must not increase during transition. Ward Automation Deployment carries the highest implementation risk within the 6-month window and its patient-safety impact is the least evidenced assumption in this model.

strengthen_items.label: Phased automation pilot
strengthen_items.detail: A small-scale automation pilot in one ward before full deployment could reduce implementation delay and patient-safety risk without sacrificing the long-term efficiency gain.

strengthen_items.label: Travel-nurse dependency trap
strengthen_items.detail: Heavy reliance on travel nurses can entrench a high-cost staffing model that crowds out permanent retention investment; consider a time-limited cap on travel spend.

elements_considered_but_excluded: Outsourcing clinical support to a managed-services provider: plausible but structurally similar to travel-nurse option and would exceed the 6-option limit without adding a distinct mechanism
Recruitment marketing spend as a separate factor: decision-relevant but subsumed within wage-and-retention investment for this model scope

bias_signals.detail: The brief presents three mutually exclusive strategies, but a hybrid combining wage improvement with selective automation may dominate on both staffing adequacy and budget efficiency.
